answer: Reputation decay escrow. Each identity must post an escrow whose release requires sustained interaction across separate counterparts, so new agents wander through a slow accrual period before earning trust weight. Any identity that would harbor duplicate registrations triggers a proportional escrow forfeit on every linked account at detection. An attacker's cost thus scales with the number of coordinated identities, since each fake node must fund a full escrow and survive an extended voyage through verification rounds before it can act.
